narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist: narration, speech introductions, glosses and his own reflections.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; calm authority, patient with those who misunderstand him.

samaritan-woman.name: The Samaritan woman
samaritan-woman.note: At Jacob's well; guarded and quick-witted, then astonished.

samaritans.name: Samaritans of Sichar
samaritans.note: Townspeople who came to believe; convinced and glad.

royal-official.name: The ruler of Capharnaum
royal-official.note: A royal official whose son is dying; urgent, pleading father.

servants.name: The ruler's servants
servants.note: Household servants bringing good news of the boy.

1.t: When Jesus therefore understood the Pharisees had heard that Jesus maketh more disciples and baptizeth more than John

2.t: (Though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples),

3.t: He left Judea and went again into Galilee.

4.t: And he was of necessity to pass through Samaria.

5.t: He cometh therefore to a city of Samaria, which is called Sichar, near the land which Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

6.t: Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well. It was about the sixth hour.

7.t: There cometh a woman of Samaria, to draw water. Jesus saith to her:

8.t: For his disciples were gone into the city to buy meats.

9.t: Then that Samaritan woman saith to him:
How dost thou, being a Jew; ask of me to drink, who am a Samaritan woman?
For the Jews do not communicate with the Samaritans.
9.q: Read as the evangelist's explanatory aside, as most editions punctuate it; it could be the woman's own words.

10.t: Jesus answered and said to her:
If thou didst know the gift of God and who he is that saith to thee: Give me to drink; thou perhaps wouldst have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.

11.t: Sir, thou hast nothing wherein to draw, and the well is deep. From whence then hast thou living water?

12.t: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank thereof, himself and his children and his cattle?

13.t: Jesus answered and said to her:
Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: but he that shall drink of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever.

14.t: But the water that I will give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting.

15.t: Sir, give me this water, that I may not thirst, nor come hither to draw.

16.t: Go, call thy husband, and come hither.

17.t: Thou hast said well: I have no husband.

18.t: For thou hast had five husbands: and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband. This, thou hast said truly.

19.t: Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.

20.t: Our fathers adored on this mountain: and you say that at Jerusalem is the place where men must adore.

21.t: Woman, believe me that the hour cometh, when you shall neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, adore the Father.

22.t: You adore that which you know not: we adore that which we know. For salvation is of the Jews.

23.t: But the hour cometh and now is, when the true adorers shall adore the Father in spirit and in truth. For the Father also seeketh such to adore him.

24.t: God is a spirit: and they that adore him must adore him in spirit and in truth.

25.t: I know that the Messias cometh
therefore, when he is come, he will tell us all things.

26.t: I am he, who am speaking with thee.

27.t: And immediately his disciples came. And they wondered that he talked with the woman. Yet no man said: What seekest thou? Or: Why talkest thou with her?
27.q: The questions are ones nobody actually asked, so the whole verse stays narration.

28.t: The woman therefore left her waterpot and went her way into the city and saith to the men there:

29.t: Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatsoever I have done. Is not he the Christ?

30.t: They went therefore out of the city and came unto him.

31.t: In the mean time, the disciples prayed him, saying:

32.t: I have meat to eat which you know not.

33.t: The disciples therefore said one to another:
Hath any man brought him to eat?

34.t: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work.

35.t: Do not you say: There are yet four months, and then the harvest cometh? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the countries. For they are white already to harvest.

36.t: And he that reapeth receiveth wages and gathereth fruit unto life everlasting: that both he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.

37.t: For in this is the saying true: That it is one man that soweth, and it is another that reapeth.

38.t: I have sent you to reap that in which you did not labour. Others have laboured: and you have entered into their labours.

39.t: Now of that city many of the Samaritans believed in him, for the word of the woman giving testimony:
He told me all things whatsoever I have done.

40.t: So when the Samaritans were come to him, they desired that he would tarry there. And he abode there two days.

41.t: And many more believed in him, because of his own word.

42.t: And they said to the woman:
We now believe, not for thy saying: for we ourselves have heard him and know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world.

43.t: Now after two days, he departed thence and went into Galilee.

44.t: For Jesus himself gave testimony that a prophet hath no honour in his own country.

45.t: And when he was come into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things he had done at Jerusalem on the festival day: for they also went to the festival day.

46.t: He came again therefore into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain ruler, whose son was sick at Capharnaum.

47.t: He having heard that Jesus was come from Judea into Galilee, sent to him and prayed him to come down and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.

48.t: Unless you see signs and wonders, you believe not.

49.t: Lord, come down before that my son die.

50.t: Go thy way. Thy son liveth.
The man believed the word which Jesus said to him and went his way.

51.t: And as he was going down, his servants met him: and they brought word, saying, that his son lived.

52.t: He asked therefore of them the hour wherein he grew better. And they said to him:
Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him.

53.t: The father therefore knew that it was at the same hour that Jesus said to him:

53.q: The narrator recalling Jesus' earlier words verbatim; given to Jesus as direct speech.

53.t: And himself believed, and his whole house.

54.t: This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judea. into Galilee.
